sections.overview: The common kestrel is a small falcon native across much of Europe, Asia and Africa.
sections.identification: Males have a grey head and tail with a chestnut back; females are more uniformly reddish-brown and barred.
sections.habitat: It commonly hunts over open grassland and farmland, and can also use urban sites.
sections.diet: Small mammals, especially voles and mice, are major prey, alongside insects and other small vertebrates.
sections.behavior: It often hovers while searching below, then drops rapidly onto prey.
sections.reproduction: It nests on ledges, in cavities or in old nests rather than building a substantial nest of its own.
sections.ecology: In some regions, small mammals dominate its diet, but prey composition varies with local availability.
sections.conservation: The global IUCN assessment cited here is Least Concern; British monitoring nevertheless reports declines, a regional trend.
